Kate (New Hire): Hi team — quick q about my start date and benefits. I start next Tues (mid-pay-cycle). How will 401k match work for my first partial paycheck? Also I enrolled in HSA during onboarding via the portal but it shows 'pending' — will employer HSA contribution be pro-rated?
Emily (People Ops): Congrats and welcome! Short answers: 401k match follows plan rules and payroll timing so match applies to contributions actually taken from payroll; partial pay may reduce the match amount that period. HSA employer contribution depends on our vendor cutover timing — sometimes it's prorated based on eligible days in the month.
Kate (New Hire): OK thanks. Is there any way to get a retroactive adjustment if my first paycheck had pre-tax elections not applied because of cutoff? My first paycheck was processed by global payroll then exported to benefits vendor and my 401k deduction didn't show up.
Raj (Payroll): Hi Kate — can you DM me your start date and the pay period dates? If payroll missed the election because of timing, depending on vendor rules we might be able to submit an off-cycle correction to add missed deferrals to the next payroll. We can't change IRS reporting for a prior year period, but within the same plan year it's sometimes fixable.
Liam (Benefits): Adding context: our 401k vendor has two cutoffs — enrollment acceptance cutoff (for enrollment feed) and contribution posting cutoff. If the enrollment didn't land before the enrollment cutoff, the vendor treats you as pending and contributions won't be pulled until next cycle. For HSA employer contributions, the vendor typically prorates by full calendar month of eligibility unless your hire date is after cutoff; in some cases we provide a one-time pro-rated employer contribution after enrollment completes.
Kate (New Hire): Is there a form I need to sign for off-cycle corrections? I clicked enroll but not sure if that counts as 'accepted' by vendor.
Emily (People Ops): Usually clicking enroll in the portal is enough, but if the feed failed we ask payroll to generate an off-cycle request. Raj will coordinate.
Raj (Payroll): If we need an off-cycle, we ask you to sign an authorization email for the makeup contribution (audit trail). Also we coordinate with Benefits to ensure match calculations exclude any ineligible earnings.
Kate (New Hire): One more thing — my offer said I'm eligible for the 'tiered match' (100% on first 3%, 50% on next 2%). How do we calculate that on partial pay?
Liam (Benefits): We calculate match per payroll period: for each paycheck we look at your deferral percentage of eligible pay that period, apply the tiered schedule to that period's contributions, then sum match across the year. So partial pay reduces the cash amount matched in that period, but the algorithm is the same. If you miss a deferral entirely due to enrollment timing, you won't get match for that pay; that's why we try to do off-cycle fixes when feasible.
Kate (New Hire): Got it — thanks. Who should I follow up with to confirm HSA employer deposit schedule?
Liam (Benefits): Follow up with me: l.benefits@redwood.example (DM if you prefer). I'll check the vendor feed timestamps and confirm if a prorated deposit is coming or if we need to request a manual credit.
PayrollBot: Reminder: off-cycle contribution requests require approval by payroll ops. Submit to #eng-payroll-ops with 'off-cycle 401k correction' and include employee ID and pay period.
Emily (People Ops): I'll add a note to your onboarding checklist so we don't lose track. Kate — feel free to tag me if you don't hear back in 48 hours. :thumbsup:
